gen-fs-excon-inter: Inter reads smooth and tube-like, its big counters opening up inside a tall lowercase. And Excon, crowded and chalky by comparison, shares that same sturdy build, which is what makes the two feel related.
gen-fs-excon-rubik: Rubik's lowercase looks big beside its capitals, soft and clear. Excon crowds its letters tight like chalk on a slate, while Rubik's open round shapes keep the text easy to follow down the page.
gen-fs-expose-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Tight, sharp, and a bit dramatic. If Expose were shrunk down, its compressed cadence would lose that punch, while Be Vietnam Pro, a plain sans with bent-rod strokes and a high mean line, holds up fine at small sizes.
gen-fs-expose-fs-familjen-grotesk: Compressed and striking, with barely a pause between letters. Expose sets the tone up top, and Familjen Grotesk follows with tall lowercase and bowls left open on one side, good for a handful of lines.
gen-fs-expose-gf-armata: Expose packs its x-height and caps almost flush, a compressed cadence that barely pauses for breath. Give Armata a little more size, since its sans-serif spacing is generous.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Refined is the first word for Expose, tightly packed and striking up top. And Noto Sans Lisu, a plain sans with wide-open s curves, gives that density somewhere to breathe.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Noto Sans Old Persian has a lofty, tall lowercase body. Expose is best at compressed, striking display lines, while the sans below does its best work letting open counters breathe.
gen-fs-expose-gf-savate: Compact, striking, and sharply cut. Savate, a sans-serif with open jaws on its curves and a tall rounded o, loosens everything up, and its light modulation only shows when you look closely.
gen-fs-expose-mulish: Mulish reads wire-like and friendly, with a large x-height and short ascenders. But if Expose were made small, its compressed cadence would lose its punch against that sans-serif body.
gen-fs-expose-poppins: Poppins is a plain sans whose lines keep their width through every turn, with a tall, sturdy lowercase. Against Expose's compressed, striking look, that steadiness is the strongest card.
